right: Set hideRoadSurfaceCRG=false whenever an overlapping road CRG is not mode=attached
Ignore object @height/@zOffset for surface elevation when <surface> is present
wrong: hideRoadSurfaceCRG=true over attached0/genuine/global road CRG
figures.formula: z = OpenDRIVE height + object CRG

figures.caption: Figure 102. Signals in ASAM OpenDRIVE
figures.shows: Perspective road (s along the centre line, t to the left) with three highlighted signal kinds: a painted zebra crossing on the road surface, a 60 speed-limit sign on a post at the right roadside, and a traffic light on a pole at the right roadside.
figures.lesson: Signals include traffic signs, traffic lights AND binding road markings (e.g. zebra crossing, painted speed limits). Non-binding road marks are objects, not signals.
right: Emit binding painted markings (stop line, zebra) as signals when they carry a rule; keep geometry as objects/roadMarks
Place signals by s/t on the road they govern
wrong: Modelling non-binding marks as signals
Signals not attached to a road

figures.caption: Figure 103. Width and height for signal
figures.shows: XML of a German speed limit sign (s=3981.4158159146, t=-14.0503, id=5000162, dynamic=no, orientation=+, zOffset=3.8835, country=DE, countryRevision=2017, type=274, subtype=100, value=100, unit=km/h, height=0.77, width=0.77, hOffset=5.7595865) next to the round 100 sign with height=0.77 m and width=0.77 m dimensioned on the sign plate itself.
figures.lesson: width/height describe the sign plate (not the post); zOffset is from the road to the bottom edge of the plate. type/subtype are only unique together with country and countryRevision; value requires unit.
right: Always write country (ISO alpha-2) with type/subtype; add countryRevision when known
Write unit whenever value is present
Recommend width/height for rendering
wrong: value without unit
zOffset measured to the sign centre
type/subtype without country

figures.caption: Figure 104. Orientation and hOffset for signal
figures.shows: Left: right-hand-traffic perspective road with reference line pointing away. Middle: 100 sign with orientation='+' and zOffset dimension from road surface to bottom of the plate. Right: top view - reference line pointing up, sign at the right roadside, red line = sign plate rotated by hOffset, measured counter-clockwise from the negative reference line direction (arrow pointing down-left). Example hOffset=5.7595865 rad (330 deg).
figures.lesson: orientation '+' means the signal applies to traffic driving in +s and with hOffset=0 its face points toward -s (toward oncoming drivers in +s). hOffset rotates counter-clockwise from that base direction; for '-' the base is +s.
right: Set orientation from which carriageway/direction the sign governs (RHT right side, +s traffic -> '+')
Compute hOffset = wrap(actual_face_heading - (road_heading + pi)) for '+', wrap(actual_face_heading - road_heading) for '-'
wrong: Using hOffset relative to +s for orientation '+'
Using orientation to restrict lanes (use validity)
figures.formula: faceHeading = roadHeading(s) + pi + hOffset (orientation '+'); faceHeading = roadHeading(s) + hOffset (orientation '-'); hOffset relative to reference line for 'none'

figures.caption: Figure 105. UML model for signals
figures.shows: UML: t_road_signals with signal 0..* and signalReference 0..* (id, orientation, s, t, validity 0..*). t_road_signals_signal: country[0..1], countryRevision[0..1], dynamic, height[0..1], hOffset[0..1], id, name[0..1], orientation, pitch[0..1], roll[0..1], s, subtype, t, text[0..1], type, unit[0..1], value[0..1], width[0..1], zOffset; children validity 0..* (fromLane, toLane), dependency 0..* (id, type[0..1]), reference 0..* (elementId, elementType, type[0..1]), physical position 0..1 = positionRoad (hOffset, pitch, roadId, roll, s, t, zOffset) or positionInertial (hdg, pitch, roll, x, y, z).
figures.lesson: Required on signal: id, s, t, zOffset, orientation, dynamic, type, subtype. Physical position is optional and exclusive (road or inertial).
right: Write subtype '-1' or 'none' when unknown (mandatory)
Use <reference elementType=signal|object> to link stop line and light
wrong: Both positionRoad and positionInertial on one signal
Missing dynamic/orientation

figures.caption: Figure 106. Lanes with signals in the shape of road marks
figures.shows: Road with lanes 4,3,2,1 (traffic leftwards) and -1,-2 (traffic rightwards). Painted speed-limit marks: 60 on lane 3, 80 on lane 2, 100 on lane 1 (all readable for leftward traffic), and 80 on lane -1 (readable for rightward traffic). Each is a separate signal.
figures.lesson: Lane-specific rules are expressed with <validity fromLane toLane> on the signal, and the validity lanes must lie on the side allowed by orientation (RHT '+' -> negative lanes, '-' -> positive lanes; LHT reversed; both sides -> 'none').
right: Use one signal per lane-specific mark with validity fromLane=toLane=laneId
Pick orientation consistent with the validity side
wrong: validity spanning positive lanes with orientation '+' in RHT
fromLane > toLane

figures.caption: Figure 107. Lane and type specific speed limit
figures.shows: Perspective two-lane road (lane 1 left, -1 right), at the right roadside a 60 sign above a supplementary plate showing a lorry. Spec XML: signal 1 (type 274 subtype 56, 60 km/h) with <dependency id=2/>; signal 2 (type 1048 subtype 12 'LorriesOnly') at the same s/t, lower zOffset.
figures.lesson: Supplementary plates are separate signals at the same position, linked by <dependency>; the semantics of the dependency type are application defined.
right: Model a sign + supplementary plate as two signals with a dependency
wrong: Encoding the supplementary plate only in the text attribute

figures.caption: Figure 108. Junction with signals at physical and logical positions
figures.shows: Four-arm junction (RHT) with green-highlighted road edges/medians and turn arrows. Traffic lights: one on a mast arm hanging over the far (north) side, one at the NE corner, one at the near SE corner, one at the near SW corner. Annotation 'logical position' points to a blue dot at the base of the SW light next to the south approach's stop line; 'physical position' lines point to the other light heads (far-side and overhead positions).
figures.lesson: The logical position (s/t on the governed road, where the rule starts) can differ from where the hardware stands. Use positionRoad (other road s/t) or positionInertial (x,y,z,hdg) for the physical location; the logical s marks the start of validity.
right: Place the signal's s/t at the stop line of the approach it governs; put the real pole location in positionInertial/positionRoad
Use positionInertial for lights hanging over a junction or on the far side
wrong: Putting a far-side light's s/t on the outgoing road (wrong road gets the rule)

figures.caption: Figure 109. UML Model Physical Position
figures.shows: UML: t_physicalPosition with positionRoad (hOffset, pitch[0..1], roadId, roll[0..1], s, t, zOffset) or positionInertial (hdg, pitch[0..1], roll[0..1], x, y, z).
figures.lesson: Physical position is either road-based or inertial, never both.
right: Choose one of positionRoad/positionInertial
wrong: Writing both

figures.caption: Figure 110. UML Model Signal Reference
figures.shows: UML: t_road_signals_signalReference (id, orientation, s, t) as 0..* child of t_road_signals (with validity 0..*).
figures.lesson: <signalReference> lets other roads (e.g. connecting roads, other lanes sharing a stop line) reuse a signal's content at their own s/t and orientation.
right: Reuse a speed limit or stop line on connecting roads via <signalReference id= s= t= orientation=>
Add validity to signalReference to restrict lanes
wrong: Duplicating identical signals with new ids on every connecting road
signalReference pointing at an object

figures.caption: Figure 111. Junction with four traffic lights, controlled by two controllers
figures.shows: Identical drawing to Figure 86: controller 1 -> NW and SE lights (N/S approaches, green), controller 2 -> NE and SW lights (E/W approaches, red).
figures.lesson: Controllers wrap the state of a group of dynamic signals; phase timing is outside OpenDRIVE.
right: Group same-phase lights under one controller
wrong: Expecting phase timing inside the .xodr

figures.caption: Figure 112. UML Model Controller
figures.shows: Same as Figure 87: t_controller (id, name[0..1], sequence[0..1]) with control 1..* (signalId, type[0..1]).
figures.lesson: Controller is a top-level element under <OpenDRIVE>.
right: Write controllers at top level, reference them from junctions
wrong: Nesting <controller> definitions inside <road>

figures.caption: Figure 113. UML Model Railroad
figures.shows: UML: t_road_railroad with switch 0..* (id, name, position e_road_railroad_switch_position) each having mainTrack (dir, id, s), sideTrack (dir, id, s) and partner 0..1 (id, name[0..1]).
figures.lesson: Rail switches live in <road><railroad><switch> on the main-track road.
right: One road per track; switches reference road ids of main and side tracks
wrong: Modelling switches as junctions

figures.caption: Figure 114. Reference lines for roads and railroads
figures.shows: Left: a road whose reference line runs along the top edge with lanes -1,-2,-3 below it. Right: a railway road with a single lane -1 whose reference line runs through the middle of the lane; laneOffset shifts the centre lane (0) up by half the lane width.
figures.lesson: For tracks the reference line must be the centre of the rail pair, so use laneOffset = +width/2 with a single rail/tram lane -1 (one rail/tram lane per road).
right: Track road: reference line = track centreline, laneOffset a=width/2, one lane type rail or tram
Lane width >= vehicle width
wrong: Putting the track reference line on the rail edge
Two rail lanes on one road
Embedding tram tracks as a lane of a street road (needs its own road)
figures.formula: laneOffset = laneWidth/2 so that the lane -1 centre coincides with the reference line

figures.caption: Figure 115. Railroad switches
figures.shows: Track 1 (dark blue, A to B, s1 to the right) and track 3 (light blue, C to D, s3 to the left). Side track 2 (s2 up-right) leaves track 1 at switch#12 and joins track 3 at switch#32. Possible connections box: A->B, A->C, B->A, C->A, C->D, D->C.
figures.lesson: Switches 12 and 32 are partners linked by side track 2; movements are only possible in the facing/trailing directions shown (no D->A or B->C). mainTrack/sideTrack give track id, s at the switch and dir for entering the side track.
right: Write a <switch> on each main track at the branch s, with <partner> when a side track links two switches
Side tracks only connect two switches
wrong: Using a main track to connect two switches
Partner on a single switch

figures.caption: Figure 116. Railroad stations
figures.shows: Top scenario: dashed station box containing one platform between track 1 (A->B) and track 3 (C->D, opposite direction); the platform is used from both tracks (one segment). Bottom scenario: station with platform 1 above track 5 (C->D) and platform 2 below the bottom track, which is split into track 4 (A to mid) and track 6 (mid to B), so platform 2 has two segments. The text numbers the bottom tracks 3/1/2 while the drawing labels them 5/4/6.
figures.lesson: A station has >=1 platform, a platform has >=1 segment, and each segment names a track road, sStart/sEnd and the side. A platform alongside a track split into two roads needs one segment per road.
right: Emit <station><platform><segment roadId sStart sEnd side>; one segment per adjacent track road
Station can also be used for bus stops
wrong: Platform without segment
Station without platform

figures.caption: Figure 117. UML Model Station

figures.lesson: paramPoly3: evaluate u(p), v(p), rotate by @hdg and translate by (@x,@y). The start tangent direction is hdg + atan2(bV, bU); p is not arc length (only endpoints match for pRange=arcLength). The curve may turn back in u, which poly3 cannot.
right: x = x0 + u*cos(hdg) - v*sin(hdg); y = y0 + u*sin(hdg) + v*cos(hdg)
Emit pRange=normalized (p in [0,1]) or arcLength explicitly
wrong: Treating p as arc length for intermediate points (lane widths/objects must use true s)
Ignoring aU/aV/bV offsets when computing the start heading
figures.formula: x(p) = x + u(p)cos(hdg) - v(p)sin(hdg); y(p) = y + u(p)sin(hdg) + v(p)cos(hdg)
figures.new: Same image as 1.7 Figure 32.

figures.caption: A cubic polynomial
figures.shows: Matplotlib plot of y(x) = 20 + 0.0005x^2 + 0.0001x^3 for x = -100..100 (y from -75 to 125), flat near y=20 around x=0.
figures.lesson: Background only: a plain cubic in x/y is single-valued y(x). The deprecated <poly3> is evaluated in a local u/v frame, not in inertial x/y.
wrong: Using inertial x as the poly3 parameter
figures.new: Same image as 1.7 Figure 26; section now marked deprecated.

figures.caption: A curve which cannot be represented by a cubic polynomial w.r.t x parameter
figures.shows: X/Y grid: a blue curve from (3,1.5) rising to the right, bulging to x~5 and turning back to (4.5, 5.1). A vertical red line at x~4.9 cuts it twice (blue markers at y~3.3 and y~4.3); warning sign 'two Y-values for one X-value'. The horizontal red line is labelled 'x' and the vertical one 'y' (labels swapped relative to their meaning).
figures.lesson: A curve that turns back in x cannot be y(x); poly3 therefore uses a local u/v frame aligned with the start heading so v(u) is single-valued. Curves that turn back even in u need paramPoly3.
right: Check monotonicity of u before choosing poly3; prefer paramPoly3 anyway
wrong: Fitting y(x) in inertial coordinates
figures.new: Same image as 1.7 Figure 27.

figures.caption: Transformation from a u/v to a x/y coordinate system with a=b=0
figures.shows: X/Y grid: start point (x(u=0), y(u=0)) at (3, 1.45) with s/t; the u axis rotated by hdg from x, v perpendicular; a curve point at (5, 4.5) with its u and v(u) projections and x(u), y(u) leaders. Text: 'Cubic polynom with a = b = 0', 'For every u-value only one v-value is possible' (check mark), and the transformation formulas.
figures.lesson: With a=b=0 the u/v frame coincides with s/t at the start; a point is start + rotation(hdg) * (u, v(u)). The figure writes this as distance sqrt(u^2+v^2) at angle hdg + arctan(v/u) - equivalent to the rotation, but implement it with the rotation matrix (atan(v/u) breaks for u<=0).
right: x = x0 + u*cos(hdg) - v*sin(hdg); y = y0 + u*sin(hdg) + v*cos(hdg)
wrong: Using arctan(v/u) without quadrant handling
figures.formula: beta = hdg + arctan(v(u)/u); x(u) = x(0) + sqrt(u^2+v(u)^2)*cos(beta); y(u) = y(0) + sqrt(u^2+v(u)^2)*sin(beta)
figures.new: Same image as 1.7 Figure 28.

figures.caption: Transformation from a u/v to a x/y coordinate system with a!=0 and b!=0
figures.shows: Same construction as Figure 31: start point offset from the u/v origin by aU, aV; start tangent at arctan(bV/bU) from u; hdg between x and u; curve doubles back to (4.8,4.8). Labels use paramPoly3 names (aU, aV, bU, bV, u(p), v(p)) although the section is about poly3 with a, b.
figures.lesson: For poly3, a non-zero a shifts the curve start off the u-axis along v and a non-zero b rotates the start tangent by arctan(b) relative to u; hdg orients the u-axis. The figure reuses paramPoly3 labels - map aV->a, bV/bU->b. Since poly3 is deprecated, a converter should just write paramPoly3 with a=b=0 (aU=aV=bV=0).
right: Keep a=b=0 (or aU=aV=bV=0) so (@x,@y,@hdg) is the true start pose
wrong: Using non-zero a/b, which makes @hdg differ from the actual start tangent and breaks continuity checks
figures.formula: v(u) = a + b*u + c*u^2 + d*u^3; start tangent angle = hdg + arctan(b)
figures.new: Same image as 1.7 Figure 29.

figures.caption: Allowed, prohibited, and recommended road linkage
figures.shows: Four panels, each two road pieces (lane 1 yellow, -1 blue, blue reference arrows). Top-left 'Gap in reference line' (red X). Top-right 'Overlap in reference line' (red X). Bottom-left reference lines meet exactly but with a heading kink, producing 'Gap in lane' on the outside and 'Overlap in lane' on the inside (warning triangle = allowed but not recommended). Bottom-right two curved pieces meeting with continuous position and tangent (green check = recommended).
figures.lesson: Linked reference lines must share the end/start point exactly (no gap, no overlap). A heading kink is tolerated but produces lane gaps/overlaps; tangent-continuous joints are recommended.
right: successor road starts exactly at predecessor end point (within tolerance ~1e-6..1e-3 m)
Match headings at joints
wrong: Small gaps/overlaps from rounding OSM nodes
Heading kinks at road joints when avoidable
figures.new: Same image as 1.7 Figure 35.

figures.caption: Allowed cases of road linkage
figures.shows: Four panels, roads @id=1 and @id=2 end to end, with link tables. Same direction: road1 successor = 2 start, road2 predecessor = 1 end (check). Both reference lines pointing away from the joint (starts touch): road1 predecessor = 2 start, road2 predecessor = 1 start (check). Both pointing toward the joint (ends touch): road1 successor = 2 end, road2 successor = 1 end (check). Bottom-right: road1 reference line at the lane 1/2 border, road2 reference line at the lane 1/-1 border, lanes line up but reference lines do not touch (red X).
figures.lesson: predecessor/successor refer to the start/end of a road's OWN reference line; contactPoint says which end of the other road is touched. Linking is valid in same, opposite and converging directions, but only if the reference lines themselves connect - matching lanes with laterally offset reference lines is not a valid link (use a consistent reference line, adjust via laneOffset within a road instead).
right: Set contactPoint start/end from which endpoint of the neighbour coincides
Keep reference-line endpoints coincident at every road-road link
wrong: Linking roads whose reference lines are laterally offset even if the lanes align
Always writing contactPoint=start for successors

figures.caption: Allowed case of road linkage within a junction
figures.shows: An incoming road with lanes -1 and -2 (reference line at its upper edge) enters a dashed junction area. Inside, one connecting road continues from the -1 lane and curves up-right (its own lane -1), another starts at the -1/-2 lane border (laterally offset from the incoming reference line) and continues straight to an outgoing road with lane -1. Green check.
figures.lesson: Splits are modelled as a junction with one connecting road per path; each connecting road has its own reference line that may start at a lane boundary of the incoming road (lane-level continuity, not reference-line identity, is what matters inside junctions).
right: One connecting road per movement, starting at the lane it continues
Link incoming road successor to the junction, connecting roads to the incoming/outgoing roads
wrong: Splitting one road into two directly via road-to-road links without a junction
figures.new: Redrawn from 1.7 Figure 37; the in-figure labels 'Connection roads' and 'Roads with junctions' were removed, otherwise same.

figures.caption: Types of elevation
figures.shows: Four panels (transparent PNG; labels black on transparent - flatten onto white to read). road elevation: z vs s profile, 'elevation along s-axis'. superelevation: cross-section rolled about s, 'elevation along t-axis'. road shape: piecewise profile with widths 1/4/3/1 m, h=0.05, 0.45, 0.0 m, slopes b=-0.10 and 0.15 m/m at t=5,4,0,-3,-4 m, 'elevation along t-axis'. cross section surface: 3D road with strips @id=2, 1, -1 and s/t/h axes, 'elevation along s-axis and t-axis'.
figures.lesson: Four independent height mechanisms: elevation(s), superelevation roll(s), shape h(s,t), and the new crossSectionSurface (polynomials in s for each t-power, per strip). s length never changes with elevation.
right: Use <elevation> for grade, superelevation for banking, and at most one lateral method per road
wrong: Combining crossSectionSurface with shape or superelevation (forbidden)
Combining shape with superelevation (deprecated)
figures.new: Redrawn from 1.7 Figure 39; NEW fourth panel 'cross section surface' (1.8.0 feature).

figures.caption: Superelevation
figures.shows: Two cross-sections in x/z. alpha = 0: flat road, t1 measured horizontally from s. alpha > 0: road rolled about s, left side up; t1 measured along t_superelevation, its horizontal projection labelled t1*cos(alpha); h tilted to h_superelevation.
figures.lesson: Superelevation is a roll angle (rad) about the reference line; positive = road falls to the right. Lane widths stay measured along the tilted surface; plan-view footprint is t*cos(alpha). Default 0. The example's reference line is parallel to y for simplicity.
right: Inward banking: a RIGHT-hand curve (right side low) gets a positive value, a LEFT-hand curve (left side low) a negative value
Plan-view lateral position = t*cos(alpha)
wrong: Interpreting superelevation as a percentage cross-fall
Pivoting about the road edge
figures.formula: y_plan = t*cos(alpha); z = elev(s) + t*sin(alpha)
figures.new: Redrawn from 1.7 Figure 40 (alpha instead of a, explicit t_superelevation/h_superelevation labels); same meaning.

figures.caption: Minimum t-definition range for road shapes
figures.shows: Plan view of a road with lanes 4..1 left and -1..-3 right whose outer edges narrow from s_R1 to s_R2. At s_R1 five shape records (circles along a vertical arrow) start from the bottom of the overall t-range; at s_R2 three records. A point (s_P, t_P) between them. A double arrow marks the 'minimum t-definition range for road shapes' = the whole t extent of the road over all s. Formulas for linear interpolation between the two profiles.
figures.lesson: Shape heights between two profile s-positions are linearly interpolated in s at the same t; each profile is a piecewise cubic in dt = t - t_record. Every profile must cover the maximum t extent of the entire road, not only the local width. Shapes interpolate linearly in s and therefore cannot follow non-linear laneOffset exactly.
right: Emit every shape profile from t_min_global to t_max_global
Order <shape> by s then t
wrong: Profiles covering only the local road width
Assuming cubic interpolation in s between profiles
figures.formula: h(sP,tP) = h_R1(tP) + (h_R2(tP) - h_R1(tP)) * (sP - sR1)/(sR2 - sR1); h_Ri(t) = a + b*dt + c*dt^2 + d*dt^3
figures.new: Redrawn from 1.7 Figure 41; the interpolation formula is CORRECTED (1.7 showed (h1+h2)*(sP-sR1)/(sR2-sR1), 1.9 shows proper linear interpolation h1 + (h2-h1)*...). Also the text adds the laneOffset caveat.

figures.caption: Road shape definition
figures.shows: Cross-section with alpha = 0: grey shape area above the flat road line, higher on the left (+t) edge at t1 and decaying toward the right; h vertical through s.
figures.lesson: Shape adds a height h(t) on top of the flat (non-superelevated) cross-section, measured vertically; the defined t-range must cover the maximum t-expansion of the whole <road>. Shapes change the actual (surface) lane width but not the plan-view width.
right: Use shape without superelevation
wrong: Leaving parts of the road without shape definition
figures.formula: z = elev(s) + h_shape(s,t)
figures.new: Split out of 1.7 Figure 42 (left panel); redrawn.

figures.caption: Road shape definition in combination with superelevation
figures.shows: Cross-section with alpha > 0: the road line rolled about s; the shape area is attached to the rolled surface (rotated with it); t1 along t_superelevation with projection t1*cos(alpha); h_superelevation tilted.
figures.lesson: When shape and superelevation are combined, the shape is rotated with the superelevation - but this combination is DEPRECATED in 1.9. A converter should use either superelevation or shape (or crossSectionSurface), not shape + superelevation.
right: Choose one lateral-profile method per road
wrong: Writing both <superelevation> and <shape> for the same road in new output
figures.new: Split out of 1.7 Figure 42 (right panel); NEW: the combination is marked deprecated.

figures.caption: Cross section surface strips on a road
figures.shows: 3D sketch of a road with lanes and a median: strip @id=2 spans the wide left part (lanes with arrows), strip @id=1 the narrow darker median band, strip @id=-1 the right part; double arrows give the extents; s/t/h axes at the near edge, t pointing left.
figures.lesson: A crossSectionSurface splits each side into up to two strips: inner (id 1 / -1, with a width) and outer (id 2 / -2, valid to the outer edge of the last lane). Strip ids and widths are independent of lane ids/widths. The outer strip may be computed relative to the inner strip's edge or independently (@mode).
right: Inner strip with <width> only if an outer strip exists on that side
Single strip per side uses id 1/-1 without width
wrong: Mapping strip ids to lane ids
Giving a width to a lone strip
figures.new: NEW in 1.8 (crossSectionSurface).

figures.caption: Cross section surface
figures.shows: Plan view along s: road reference line in the middle. Labelled bands from top: strip 2 'outer left' up to 'end of outer left lane definition'; strip 1 with 'width inner left' up to 'end of inner left strip definition'; the 'start of inner strips (t_off)' line above the reference line; strip -1 'width inner right' down to 'end of inner right strip definition'; strip -2 'outer right' to 'end of outer right lane definition'. tOffset grows from 0 at the start, shifting the inner strips' origin off the reference line.
figures.lesson: Strip geometry: tOffset(s) shifts the split point between left and right strips; inner widths w(s) are cubics in s; outer strips run to the road's outer lane edge. Height = co(s) + li(s)*dt + qu(s)*dt^2 + cu(s)*dt^3 where each of co/li/qu/cu is its own piecewise cubic in s and dt is measured from tOffset (inner) or from the inner strip edge (outer). Must start at s=0 and cover the full road; lane @height is added on top; cannot be combined with shape or superelevation.
right: First <coefficients> at s=0 for tOffset, width and each component
relative mode: h_outer = h_inner(edge) + h_outer(dt)
wrong: Combining with <shape>/<superelevation>
Starting coefficients at s>0
figures.formula: t_eff = t - tOffset(s); inner: dt = t_eff; outer left: dt = t_eff - w_left; outer right: dt = t_eff + w_right; h = co(s) + li(s)dt + qu(s)dt^2 + cu(s)dt^3 (spec text writes the outer-left condition as t_eff < w_left - a typo for t_eff > w_left)
figures.new: NEW in 1.8 (crossSectionSurface).

figures.caption: Road surface as defined in a CRG file
figures.shows: Rendered 3D patch of road with kerbs on both sides: cobblestone section at the far end, smooth asphalt in front with a pothole, dashed centre marking.
figures.lesson: OpenCRG provides detailed surface relief (and optionally friction) on a regular curved grid; it complements, not replaces, the lane model and carries no visual data.
right: Reference CRG via <surface><CRG file=...> only when such data exists
wrong: Expecting CRG to define lanes or appearance
figures.new: Same image as 1.7 Figure 43.

figures.caption: ASAM OpenCRG road surface description using u/v coordinates and x/y coordinates
figures.shows: MATLAB output for belgian_block-txt-double.crg: CRG reference line in X/Y (226..234, 78..84), XYZ surface plot in the curved grid (heights 2.04-2.18 m), and UVZ map in the uncurved u/v grid (u 730-740, v -1.5..1.5) showing paving blocks.
figures.lesson: CRG has its own reference line and (u,v) coordinates analogous to (s,t); combining with OpenDRIVE needs a mapping between the two reference lines and a rule for heights.
right: Map u = s - sOffset, v = t - tOffset in attached modes
wrong: Assuming CRG u starts at 0
figures.new: Same image as 1.7 Figure 44.

figures.caption: Positioning of an ASAM OpenCRG file along the reference line
figures.shows: s/t plane: road (left yellow, right blue) with the reference line along s; a CRG grid patch from s_Start to s_End whose own reference line (black arrow) is shifted to the right of the road reference line by t_Offset.

right: Set sStart/sEnd to the CRG data extent
wrong: Applying CRG data outside [sStart, sEnd]
figures.new: Same image as 1.7 Figure 45.

figures.caption: ASAM OpenCRG attachment mode, attached
figures.shows: s/t axes with the CRG u/v axes shifted by sOffset along s and tOffset along t; the coloured CRG height map is laid along s, label 'attached'.
figures.lesson: attached: the CRG reference line is replaced by the OpenDRIVE reference line; CRG geometry (position, heading, curvature, elevation, superelevation) is discarded; CRG heights (scaled, offset) are ADDED to the OpenDRIVE surface height.
right: (u,v) = (s - sOffset, t - tOffset) for orientation=same
wrong: Using the CRG's own XY reference line in attached mode

figures.new: Same image as 1.7 Figure 46.

figures.caption: ASAM OpenCRG attached mode with elevation
figures.shows: Side view: blue road elevation profile rising; vertical bars at s_Start, s_Offset and s_End; the 'CRG Data' band (dark blue) rides on top of the rising elevation from s_Offset onward; 'OpenCRG projected on reference line'.

right: totalHeight = crg(u,v)*zScale + zOffset + laneHeightNoCRG(s,t)
wrong: Replacing the elevation by CRG heights in attached mode

right: sEnd = sOffset + CRG data length
wrong: sEnd beyond data in attached0/genuine modes

figures.new: Same image as 1.7 Figure 48.

figures.caption: ASAM OpenCRG attachment mode, genuine
figures.shows: s/t axes; the CRG start placed at (sOffset, tOffset) and its u axis rotated by hOffset; the CRG reference line curves independently of s; label 'genuine'.
figures.lesson: genuine: CRG start point is positioned relative to the reference-line point given by sStart/sOffset/tOffset and rotated by hOffset; CRG geometry is used as-is (does not bend with the OpenDRIVE line) and CRG absolute heights replace OpenDRIVE heights. Geometries must match within tolerance.

wrong: Using genuine for synthetic roads whose geometry differs from the CRG track
figures.new: Same image as 1.7 Figure 49.

figures.caption: ASAM OpenCRG orientation
figures.shows: Two panels. orientation=same: CRG grid with corners A (top-left), B, C, D, origin u=0,v=0 at s_Start shifted by t_Offset below the reference line, u along +s, v along +t. orientation=opposite: the same grid rotated 180 deg about its origin (letters drawn upside down, A bottom-right), extending toward -s from s_Start, u pointing -s and v pointing -t; t_Offset unchanged.
figures.lesson: orientation=opposite rotates the CRG by 180 deg about its u/v origin: both u and v reverse relative to s and t; tOffset is not affected. Note the printed matrix [[0,-1],[-1,0]] would swap u and v - it should be [[-1,0],[0,-1]] for a 180 deg rotation (same error as in 1.7).

wrong: Implementing the printed matrix literally (swaps u and v)

figures.caption: Figure 57. Center lane for road with lanes of different driving directions
figures.shows: Two-way road, reference line (blue solid arrow, pointing right) coincides with the centre lane 0 (blue dash-dot, drawn a few px above it only for visibility). Left (tan) lanes 3,2,1; lane 3 is separated from 2 by a white gap (a narrow outer lane, e.g. border). Right (blue) lanes -1,-2. No lane offset.

right: Centre lane 0 equals the reference line when there is no laneOffset
New lane starts at width 0 at the section start and widens with the cubic
Outer lanes keep their geometry but get new ids after an inserted lane
wrong: Matching lanes across a section boundary by id instead of by lateral position
Giving the centre lane a width

figures.caption: Figure 58. Center lane for road with lanes of identical driving direction
figures.shows: One-way road: reference line (blue arrow pointing right) at the right edge, centre lane 0 on it, only left lanes 1,2 (dashed separator) and an outer lane 3 behind a white gap. Hollow arrows in lanes 1 and 2 point LEFT, i.e. against the reference line, which is the RHT default for left lanes. No right lanes.
figures.lesson: A one-way road can be modelled with all lanes on one side of the centre lane; the side together with the road's traffic rule fixes the driving direction.
right: One-way road with only <left> (or only <right>) lanes
Left lanes in RHT drive against s
Prefer right lanes with the reference line along traffic for OSM oneway=yes so the default direction is correct without @direction
wrong: Placing lanes on both sides of a one-way road and relying on @direction to fix it
Forgetting that left lanes in RHT run against s
figures.new: Unchanged from 1.7 Figure 53. 1.8+ adds @direction (standard/reversed/both) to override the side-based default.

figures.caption: Figure 59. UML class diagram of the Lanes class
figures.shows: UML: t_road_lanes has @layer (e_layerType, default permanent) and two constraints: (1) if layer is permanent then laneSection/@length is not allowed; (2) if any laneOffset exists then no laneSection//border. Children: laneOffset 0..* (s,a,b,c,d) and laneSection 1..* (length 0..1, s, singleSide 0..1). laneSection has center 1, left 0..1, right 0..1. Center lane: id=0, type and level marked DEPRECATED. Left lane id positiveInteger, right lane id negativeInteger; both derive from t_road_lanes_laneSection_lr_lane with type, advisory (default none), direction (default standard), dynamicLaneType, dynamicLaneDirection, level, roadWorks (default false). lane children: link 0..1 (predecessor/successor 0..* with id and layer default permanent), roadMark 0..*, height 0..*, LaneGeometry xor-choice width 1..* | border 1..*, rule, material (sOffset, surface, friction, roughness), speed (sOffset, max, unit), access 0..* (sOffset, rule, deprecated restriction attr; child restriction 0..* with type).
figures.lesson: Schema-level: <lanes> may occur twice per road (permanent + temporary layer); width and border are mutually exclusive per lane; laneOffset excludes border; centre lane no longer carries type/level.
right: <lanes> without @layer = permanent
Use <access rule=...><restriction type=.../></access> children
Every lane needs width (or border) from sOffset 0
wrong: Writing @type on the centre lane in a 1.9 file (deprecated)
Mixing <width> and <border>
laneOffset together with border
@length on a permanent lane section

figures.caption: Figure 60. Road with two lane layers "permanent" (white markings) and "temporary" (yellow markings) in a roadworks setting
figures.shows: 3D rendering of a motorway roadworks zone: white permanent markings stay in place while yellow temporary markings swing across them; red/white beacons block parts of the permanent lanes. On the right carriageway an outer permanent lane is blocked; on the left a permanent inner lane is closed for its own direction but a temporary lane on top of it carries traffic of the OPPOSITE carriageway (contraflow). Concrete barrier separates the old carriageways.
figures.lesson: Temporary lanes are an overlay with their own lane ids, sections, offset and markings; they take precedence for driving but inherit surface/height from the permanent layer.
right: Mark blocked permanent lanes with @roadWorks=true
Temporary layer total width (per lane group) <= permanent
Temporary lanes have no <height>/<material>
wrong: Rebuilding the permanent geometry for a roadworks zone
Letting a temporary lane extend outside the permanent surface
figures.new: New in 1.8 (lane layers). Not present in 1.7.

figures.caption: Figure 61. Example with lanes on the permanent and temporary lane layer
figures.shows: Rendered road view: near section has only permanent lanes (white solid edge lines, white dashed centre). Further away yellow temporary lines branch off the white ones: on the left the yellow edge bends inward, the yellow dashed lane line shifts sideways, on the right a yellow edge line bends outward onto the shoulder. XML excerpt: permanent and temporary layers both have a laneSection at s=40 with right lanes -1 median 2.0, -2 border 0.75, -3/-4 driving 3.75, -5 border, -6 stop 3.0, -7 shoulder 1.5; permanent lanes list successor on BOTH layers (successor id=-3 layer=permanent and successor id=-3 layer=temporary); temporary lanes use cubic widths (c,d non-zero) to shift.

right: link/successor@layer to jump between layers
Start a permanent lane section wherever a temporary section starts/ends
Shift temporary lanes with their own cubic width or laneOffset
wrong: Linking layers without a permanent lane-section break
Omitting the layer link so the temporary lanes are unreachable

figures.caption: Figure 62. Lane grouping with left, center, right
figures.shows: Braces group lanes 3,2,1 as 'left', lane 0 on the reference line as 'center', -1,-2 as 'right'. Hollow arrows: lanes 1 and 2 point against s (left), lane -1 along s (right) -> RHT. Lanes 3 and -2 are narrow outer strips without arrows.

figures.caption: Figure 64. Lane sections defined separately for both sides of the road

wrong: Linking a widening-from-zero lane

P (orange) inside square C3,0-C4,0-R4,0-R3,0 (black). 12 neighbours: L2,0..L5,0 (left row), C2,0 and C5,0 (yellow), R2,0 and R5,0 (blue), R2,1..R5,1 (second right row). 4x4 stencil spans rows L,C,R0,R1 and columns 2..5. figures.section: 12.11.2 Interpolation between incoming road and elevation grid
figures.caption: Figure 106. Three segments of a junction boundary and the corner points P0, P1, P2, and P3 of the polygon at an incoming road
figures.shows: Close-up of the south arm: dashed red joint segment across the road end (sidewalk brown at left, lanes tan/blue, blue reference line arrow pointing into junction). P0 and P1 are the joint's endpoints on the boundary; P3 and P2 lie @transitionLength further along the adjacent lane segments (into the junction). Point P inside the quadrilateral; grid points and grid lines in grey.

right: Set transitionLength on joints of incoming roads (default 0 = hard step)
wrong: transitionLength 0 with non-matching grid z (creates a step)

figures.section: 12.11.2 Interpolation between incoming road and elevation grid
figures.caption: Figure 107. Polygon and the lines AB and CD through the point P
figures.shows: Quadrilateral P0 (bottom left), P1 (bottom right), P2 (top right), P3 (top left). Red lines through P: A on P0P1 to B on P3P2, and C on P0P3 to D on P1P2. Only AB is used by the formulas; CD is drawn but unused.
figures.lesson: Find bilinear parameters k (along joint) and l (from road towards grid) of P, take z and slope from the road at A and from the grid at B, then cubic Hermite in l.
right: Solve the 2x2 bilinear system for k,l
wrong: Text typo: gradient at B is also called m_A; it is m_B
figures.formula: A = P0 + k(P1-P0); B = P3 + k(P2-P3); P = A + l(B-A) -> m*k*l + n*k + o*l + p = 0 and q*k*l + r*k + s*l + t = 0 (m=x2-x3-x1+x0, n=x1-x0, o=x3-x0, p=x0-xP; same with y); z_P(l) = a + b*l + c*l^2 + d*l^3 with a=zA, b=mA, c=-3zA+3zB-2mA-mB, d=2zA-2zB+mA+mB, gradients normalised by |AB|

figures.caption: Figure 108. Junction group with three junctions

Large dashed red box = junctionGroup id A enclosing everything.

right: One small junction per roundabout arm
Group them with type roundabout
wrong: One giant junction for the whole roundabout
Ring roads as connecting roads
figures.new: Same picture as 1.7 Figure 84.

figures.shows: UML: t_junctionGroup (name 0..1, id, type e_junctionGroup_type) with junctionReference 1..* (junction: string).

right: type required

figures.caption: Figure 110. Example of a junction with 20 traffic lights mapped into six signal groups (IDs 42-47)
figures.shows: drawio SVG without text nodes (labels are drawn as paths); viewed by rendering it with headless Chrome. right: One controller per signal group, all listed in the junction
Pedestrian and tram signals get their own groups
wrong: Junction controllers on virtual junctions

figures.caption: Figure 111. Circular and angular object
figures.shows: Road with reference line on top (s to the right, t up) and right lanes -1,-2,-3 below. A circular object with centre M at (s1, t1) beside lane -3, radius r. A rectangular object at (s2, t2) inside lane -3 with local u axis along s and v axis along t; 'length' is dimensioned along u, 'width' along v. t values are measured from the reference line (negative, to the right).
figures.lesson: An object is placed by the (s, t, zOffset) of its origin, which is the centre of its bounding volume. Shape is EITHER radius (+height, cylinder) OR length+width (+height, box). In 1.9 the attribute table now agrees with the drawing: @length is along local u (road direction when hdg=0), @width along local v (lateral).
right: Write s,t,zOffset of the bounding-volume centre, not of a corner
Use length along u (s direction at hdg=0) and width along v (t direction)
Use radius only for round items (trees, poles, bollards); never combine radius with length/width
Make every point of the real object lie inside the bounding volume, and each face of the box touch the object
wrong: Swapping length and width (the 1.7 table had them reversed)
Giving both radius and width/length
Placing the origin at the object footprint edge
figures.new: Same drawing as 1.7 Figure 88, but 1.9 fixes the text inconsistency: length=u-axis, width=v-axis, height along z of the local frame. New object attributes @temporary and @invalidated (1.9).

figures.caption: Figure 112. Placing objects on roads
figures.shows: Side view z over s: road elevation (blue) is flat then rises in an S-shape. A long grey slab is inserted with its origin on the curve: its rear end dips below the flat road start, its front end cuts into the rising road while the middle floats above the dip.

right: Split long on-road features (painted areas, long islands) into short objects or use a repeat (which follows the road)
Use cornerRoad outlines with per-corner dz/height so the outline follows the surface
Use perpToRoad only for objects smaller than the vertical curvature radius
wrong: One long rigid object over a crest or sag
Relying on pitch/roll to fix a long object on a curved profile
figures.new: Same idea as 1.7 Figure 90; 1.9 adds the explicit warning about skewed OpenCRG surfaces and the 1.9 rule avoid_skewed_crg_surfaces tied to @perpToRoad.

figures.caption: Figure 113. UML class diagram of the Objects class
figures.shows: t_road_objects contains object 0..*, objectReference 0..*, tunnel 0..*, bridge 0..*. t_road_objects_object: required s (grEqZero), t, zOffset, id; optional type (e_objectType), subtype, name, dynamic (yes/no), validLength, orientation, hdg, pitch, roll, height (>=0), length (>0), width, radius (>0), perpToRoad, invalidated=false, temporary=false. Children: repeat 0..*, material 0..*, laneValidity 0..* (fromLane, toLane, layer=permanent), parkingSpace 0..1 (access, restrictions), markings 0..1 -> marking 1..* (side, weight, width, color, zOffset, spaceLength, lineLength, startOffset, stopOffset) -> cornerReference 0..* (id), borders 0..1 -> border 1..* (width, type, outlineId, useCompleteOutline), surface 0..1 -> CRG 0..1 (file, hideRoadSurfaceCRG, zScale), skeleton 0..1 -> polyline 1..* (id) -> choice vertexRoad 2..* (s,t,dz,radius,intersectionPoint,id) xor vertexLocal 2..* (u,v,z,radius,intersectionPoint,id), outlines 0..1 -> outline 1..* (id, fillType, outer=true, closed, laneType) and legacy outline 0..1; outline geometry xor: cornerRoad 2..* (s,t,dz,height,id) | curveLocal 1..* (u,v,z,height,length,hdg,id; one of line / arc(curvature) / paramPoly3(aU..dV,pRange)) | cornerLocal 2..* (u,v,z,height,id). tunnel: s,length,name,id,type,lighting,daylight. bridge: s,length,name,id,type. objectReference: s,t,id,zOffset,validLength,orientation. Constraint block lists per-type forbidden children (e.g. crosswalk: no skeleton/border/radius, repeat only distance 0; pole: no border/parking/material/marking, repeat only distance>0; tree/vegetation/building analogous) and the xor of radius vs width+length. markings constraint: markings directly under object only when no outline; marking with side cannot have cornerReference, otherwise >=2 cornerReference.
figures.lesson: This is the authoritative data model for <objects>. Key rules for a writer: shape xor (radius | width+length), outline geometry xor (cornerRoad | cornerLocal | curveLocal), markings live under <object> only without outline and under <outline> when an outline exists, laneValidity is the same class used by signals and carries a layer.
right: Model objects as a struct with required s,t,zOffset,id and optional everything else
Emit <outlines><outline> (not the legacy single <outline>) for new files
Keep corner ids starting at 0 and incrementing by 1 when markings reference them
Respect per-type forbidden children (e.g. no <borders> except on trafficIsland)
Add @temporary/@invalidated only when true (defaults false)
wrong: Mixing cornerRoad and cornerLocal in one outline
Putting <markings> under <object> while the object also has an outline
Giving a pole/tree a continuous repeat (distance=0)
Using <borders> on non-trafficIsland objects
figures.new: Much larger than 1.7 Figure 89: adds skeleton/polyline/vertexRoad/vertexLocal (1.8), curveLocal with line/arc/paramPoly3 (1.9), outline.outer/closed/laneType, surface/CRG, laneValidity.layer (1.9), object.invalidated/temporary (1.9), repeat.detachFromReferenceLine and bT/cT/dT (1.9), and an explicit per-type constraint list.

figures.caption: Figure 114. Traffic island as object
figures.shows: Road with outer lanes 3 and -3 (dark red, non-driving), lanes 2 (traffic to the left) and -2 (traffic to the right). Around the reference line the boundary between lanes 2 and -2 opens into a lens; the lens is filled with orange hatched chevron area and in its middle sits a green rounded island with a dark-red pedestrian refuge strip crossing it.
figures.lesson: A traffic island inside a road is an object (type trafficIsland) described by several outlines: one outer outline (the whole lens) and inner outlines (green body, refuge) fully inside it, each with its own fillType/laneType. The surrounding lanes widen around it rather than the island cutting the lanes.
right: Exactly one outline with outer=true; all inner outlines fully inside it
Where an inner outline touches the outer one, share the identical point
Use fillType (grass, paint, pavement...) and laneType per outline
Use cornerRoad or curveLocal for smooth island shapes
wrong: Several outer outlines on one object
Inner outline sticking out of the outer outline
Modelling the island as a lane with no width transition around it
figures.new: Same drawing as 1.7 Figure 94; 1.9 adds the rules exactly_one_outer and inner_outline_touches_outer and the explanation of multiple outlines (pedestrian refuge, curb).

figures.caption: Figure 115. Object described by corner road coordinates
figures.shows: Inertial X/Y grid; S-shaped road from about (10,10) to (45,55) with perpendicular s ticks every 10 m (s=0..80) and the local s/t axes at s=0. Beside it a 9-corner concave polygon with corners [s1,t1]..[s9,t9] listed counter-clockwise.
figures.lesson: cornerRoad corners are given in road coordinates (s, t, dz, height), but in 1.9 the edges between consecutive corners are straight lines in the INERTIAL system (corners are first converted to x,y,z, then linearly interpolated). The outline does not bend between corners; to follow a curved road, add more corners.
right: Convert each corner (s,t,dz) to x,y,z first, then connect linearly
Densify corners along curved roads
List area corners counter-clockwise
Use id 0,1,2,... when markings reference corners
wrong: Interpolating the edge in s/t space (that would bend the edge with the road)
Fewer than 2 cornerRoad points
Mixing cornerRoad with cornerLocal/curveLocal in one outline
figures.formula: e(p) = P_i + (P_{i+1} - P_i) * p, with P = (x,y,z) of corner after road->inertial transform, p in [0,1]
figures.new: The 1.7 lesson 'outline bends with the road' is replaced: 1.9 states edges are straight in inertial coordinates. New 1.9 rules: first_id_zero, sequential_id_values, mandatory id when markings exist.

figures.caption: Figure 116. An object described by <cornerLocal> coordinates
figures.shows: Curved road from about (15,70); s ticks 0..50. A green arrow goes from the reference line at s=20 to the object origin P (s=20, t=-30, zOffset=0, hdg=7pi/4 rad). At P a local u/v frame rotated by hdg; the same 9-corner polygon is given as [u1,v1]..[u9,v9].
figures.lesson: cornerLocal corners are in the object's local u/v/z frame: origin = (s,t,zOffset) of the object, rotated by hdg relative to the road heading at s. The shape is rigid and independent of road curvature; ideal for buildings and islands defined from polygons.
right: Compute origin from s,t; heading = road heading(s) + hdg; transform polygon into u/v
Store z per corner relative to the origin
Use for OSM building/area polygons (convert x,y to u,v around a chosen centroid)
wrong: Treating hdg as an inertial heading (it is relative to the road)
Using cornerLocal for long features that must follow the road
figures.formula: x = x0 + u*cos(H) - v*sin(H), y = y0 + u*sin(H) + v*cos(H), H = roadHdg(s) + hdg
figures.new: Same as 1.7 Figure 96; 1.9 adds id rules and the exclusivity rule including curveLocal.

figures.caption: Figure 117. An object described by <cornerLocal> coordinates using <paramPoly3> elements
figures.shows: Same road and origin P (s=20, t=-30, zOffset=0, hdg=7pi/4) as Figure 116, but the outline is a smooth blob: straight segments [u1,v1]->[u2,v2]->[u3,v3]->[u4,v4], then a large smooth curve from [u4,v4] round to [u5,v5] and a concave curve to [u6,v6] before a straight edge back.
figures.lesson: New 1.9 curveLocal: each outline vertex starts a curve (line, arc with constant curvature, or paramPoly3 in u/v) with @hdg and optional @length; the curve must end exactly at the next vertex (continuity). This gives smooth traffic islands and painted shapes without dense polygons.
right: Use curveLocal with arc for round island noses, paramPoly3 for measured shapes
Ensure each curve ends at the next vertex (continuous_curve_local)
Set pRange (arcLength or normalized) consistently with coefficients
Make @length match the integrated curve length
wrong: Mixing curveLocal with cornerLocal/cornerRoad in one outline
Leaving gaps between successive curves
Using normalized coefficients with p up to length
figures.formula: u(p)=aU+bU p+cU p^2+dU p^3, v(p)=aV+bV p+cV p^2+dV p^3; arc: constant curvature (positive = left/CCW)
figures.new: Entirely new in 1.9 (no 1.7 counterpart). Caption wording says cornerLocal but the section is curveLocal.

figures.caption: Figure 118. Example of the bounding volume and skeleton of a traffic light pole
figures.shows: Perspective road (s up the image, t to the left). A traffic-light pole object at @s=25, @t=1.5 with bounding box width=3 (along t), length=0.3 (along s), height=4. Inside the box: polyline id=1 is the vertical pole whose bottom vertex is marked 'intersection point' (touches ground); polyline id=2 is the arm, kinking from the pole and running horizontally across over the road.

right: Model mast-arm traffic light poles as pole/trafficLight with a skeleton: polyline for mast (first vertex intersectionPoint) and polyline for arm
Keep all vertices and their radius boundaries inside the bounding box
Use the same parameter style (radius OR width+length) for all vertices of one polyline
wrong: Bounding box that does not cover the arm
Mixing vertexRoad and vertexLocal in one polyline
Using radius and width/length on the same vertex
figures.new: New since 1.8 (skeleton absent in 1.7). Also illustrates that width is along t and length along s for objects.

figures.caption: Figure 119. Example of the skeleton of a tree
figures.shows: Road on the left (s up, t left). A tree at @s=9, @t=-5, @zOffset=-1 to the right of the road. Large grey bounding box; inside, polyline id=1 is the thin trunk (cylinder) whose lower vertex is the intersection point with the ground (zOffset below road level), polyline id=2 is the crown drawn as a wide cylinder on top.

right: Use type=tree with radius bounding cylinder or box, plus optional skeleton trunk+crown
Mark the ground contact vertex with intersectionPoint=true
wrong: Single opaque bounding box only, when clearance under the crown matters
Vertices outside the bounding box
figures.new: New since 1.8. Replaces the 1.7 suggestion of two outlines for trunk/crown with the more natural skeleton (outlines also remain possible).

figures.caption: Figure 120. Large angular continuous object with changing shape using a single <repeat> element
figures.shows: Top view: curved two-lane road (lanes -1, -2). A blue continuous band starts at s (tStart, widthStart) and runs 'length' along the reference line to tEnd/widthEnd, following the curve and narrowing; its centre dash-dot line moves closer to the road. Side view: band height shrinks from heightStart to heightEnd while zOffset rises from zOffsetStart to zOffsetEnd.

right: Use distance=0 for guard rails, walls, fences, hedges
Set tStart/tEnd, widthStart/End, heightStart/End, zOffsetStart/End
Set detachFromReferenceLine=true only for a straight segment that should not follow the road
wrong: Continuous repeat for objects with outline or skeleton changing dimensions
Using widthStart/End on a radius-defined object
figures.formula: a(ds) = aStart + (aEnd - aStart) * ds/length
figures.new: Same picture as 1.7 Figure 91; 1.9 adds detachFromReferenceLine semantics and cubic t (bT,cT,dT).

figures.caption: Figure 121. Repeated small angular objects with changing shape using a single <repeat> element

figures.lesson: Logically linked drivable lanes must meet with matching x,y (no horizontal gap), matching heading (no kink), matching z and roll (no vertical gap) and should match pitch (no vertical kink), within floating tolerance.
right: Check every predecessor/successor link: position, heading, z, roll, pitch at lane-edge touching points
Account for reference line direction (contactPoint start/end) when comparing headings
Fix geometry, not just links
wrong: Linking roads whose ends are separated or overlap
Linking roads that meet at an angle
figures.formula: match(|p1-p2| < eps_xy, |hdg1-hdg2| < eps_hdg, |z1-z2| < eps_z, |roll1-roll2| < eps)
figures.new: New normative annex in 1.8/1.9; formalises what 1.7 left implicit.

figures.caption: Figure 149. Touching Points within laneSections
figures.shows: One road with lane sections A, B, C. A laneOffset transition in B moves the centre lane up by 'Lane offset' relative to the reference line; lane ids renumber between sections (e.g. 2,1,-1 in A; 2,1/0/-1,-2 in B; 1,-1,-2 in C), outer green border lanes 3/-2 -> 3/-3 -> 2/-3. Red touching points sit on each lane boundary at section borders.
figures.lesson: Smoothness must also hold at lane-section boundaries inside one road: lane edges in consecutive sections must meet without gaps/kinks; laneOffset must be smooth across the boundary.
right: Check lane-edge continuity at every laneSection boundary
Ensure lane links between sections pair lanes whose edges coincide
Keep laneOffset continuous (value and slope)
wrong: Width jumps at section boundaries
laneOffset with discontinuous value or derivative

figures.caption: Figure 150. Touching Points for connecting roads
figures.shows: Incoming road with lanes -1,-2 enters a dashed junction area; two connecting roads (lane -1 each) leave: one curves up-right into an outgoing road, one straight. Touching points at start and end of each connecting road coincide with incoming/outgoing lane edges. Marked correct.
figures.lesson: Connecting roads must start exactly at the incoming lane edges and end exactly at the outgoing lane edges with matching heading.
right: Fit connecting road geometry to the touching points and headings of both ends
Validate every connection's both ends
wrong: Connecting road starting at the reference line of the incoming road when its lane is offset

figures.caption: Figure 151. Touching Points for multiple lane linkage
figures.shows: Aerial road photo: lane -1 splits into lanes -1 (left-turn arrow) and -2 (right-turn arrow). Red touching points on the outer edges; a yellow point at the start of the new dividing line labelled 'Not a Touching Point' because lane -1 has two successors.
figures.lesson: When a lane has multiple successors (lane split), the internal point where the new divider starts is not a touching point; only the outer edges are checked. Horizontal gaps cannot exist between adjacent lanes by construction.
right: Allow one lane to have two successors at a split; check outer edges only
wrong: Flagging a smoothness error at the inner split point

figures.figure: UML Core (ch. 6.3 root element / ch. 7 additional data)
figures.caption: UML class diagram 'Core' (OpenDRIVE root and g_additionalData)
figures.shows: OpenDRIVE::t_OpenDRIVE contains header (1), road 1..*, vmsGroup 0..*, controller 0..*, junction 0..*, junctionGroup 0..*, station 0..*; all classes specialise _OpenDriveElement which carries g_additionalData 0..*: userData 0..* (code, value[0..1], any content), include 0..* (file), dataQuality 0..1 (error 0..1: xyAbsolute, zAbsolute, xyRelative, zRelative; rawData 0..1: date, source, sourceComment[0..1], postProcessing, postProcessingComment[0..1]). Simple types t_zeroOne, t_grEqZero, t_grZero (double) and union t_grEqZeroOrContactPoint.
figures.lesson: Element order under <OpenDRIVE>: header, road+, then vmsGroup/controller/junction/junctionGroup/station. Every element may carry userData/include/dataQuality. At least one road is required.
right: Write header first, then roads, then controllers, junctions, junctionGroups, stations
Use dataQuality rawData source='sensor'/'custom' + postProcessing for OSM-derived data
Put OSM ids in userData (code='osm_id')
wrong: File with zero roads
Custom attributes instead of userData
figures.new: 1.9 adds vmsGroup at top level (1.8) and t_grEqZeroOrContactPoint union for junction boundaries.

figures.caption: UML class diagram 'Header'
figures.shows: t_header: revMajor, revMinor (integer), name, version, date, north, south, east, west, vendor (all [0..1]); children geoReference 0..1, offset 0..1 (x,y,z,hdg), license 0..1 (name, spdxid[0..1], text[0..1], resource[0..1]), defaultRegulations 0..1 -> roadRegulations 0..* (type e_roadType) and signalRegulations 0..* (type, subtype), each with semantics 0..1.
figures.lesson: Header can now declare a license (useful for ODbL OSM data) and default regulations per road type with semantics (e.g. default urban speed).
right: revMajor=1, revMinor=9
Add <license name='ODbL-1.0' spdxid='ODbL-1.0'> for OSM-derived maps
Use defaultRegulations to state default speed per road type instead of placing signs everywhere
wrong: Omitting geoReference when coordinates are projected
figures.new: license and defaultRegulations are new since 1.8.

figures.caption: UML class diagram 'Road'
figures.shows: t_road: name[0..1], length (grZero), id {id}, junction (string), rule e_trafficRule[0..1]; children link 0..1, type 0..* (s, type e_roadType, country[0..1]) -> speed 0..1 (max t_maxSpeed = number or string, unit), planView 1, elevationProfile 0..1, lateralProfile 0..1, lanes 1..2, objects 0..1, signals 0..1, surface 0..1, railroad 0..1. e_countryCode accepts ISO alpha-2 (alpha-3 deprecated).
figures.lesson: Road has exactly one planView and one or two <lanes> (second for a lane layer), optional objects/signals/railroad. rule sets RHT/LHT per road.
right: Write @rule='RHT' (or LHT) explicitly
junction='-1' for non-junction roads
Use 2-letter country codes
wrong: Two <lanes> without distinct layers
Alpha-3 country codes
figures.new: lanes multiplicity 1..2 (lane layers) and rule attribute are newer than 1.7's single lanes.

figures.caption: UML class diagram 'RoadGeometry'
figures.shows: planView -> geometry 1..* (s, x, y, hdg, length>0) with one of line, spiral (curvStart, curvEnd), arc (curvature), poly3 (deprecated; a,b,c,d), paramPoly3 (aU..dV, pRange). elevationProfile -> elevation 0..* (s,a,b,c,d). lateralProfile with constraint crossSectionSurface xor (superelevation/shape): superelevation 0..* (s,a,b,c,d), shape 0..* (s,t,a,b,c,d), crossSectionSurface 0..1 -> tOffset 0..1, surfaceStrips 1 -> strip 1..4 (id, mode) each with width/constant/linear/quadratic/cubic 0..1 -> coefficients 1..* (s,a,b,c,d). surface -> CRG 0..* (file, sStart, sEnd, orientation, mode, purpose, sOffset, tOffset, xOffset, yOffset, zOffset, zScale, hOffset).

right: Emit line/arc/spiral/paramPoly3 only
